newsitem.title: CANADA: Union official says Burns layoffs likely seasonal.
newsitem.headline: Union official says Burns layoffs likely seasonal.

text.p: Canada's largest food processor, Maple Leaf Foods Inc last week gave 100 of its Burns Meats pork packer unit employees layoff notices in what union leaders described as a "seasonal" move.

"I think this is really just part of the annual cycle. When people start barbequing in April, business will pick up," United Food and Commercial Workers local 832 spokesman Don Keith said. "We typically expect in February and March there will be layoffs at Burns."
The Burns plant is located in Winnipeg and employs 800 people, many of whom are represented by UFCW local 832.
"We're ninety percent sure these layoffs are not related to the hog dispute although the company might try to say they are because of the hog price dispute," Keith said.

He referred to ongoing negotiations between Maple Leaf and Manitoba Pork on a new pricing formula to ensure hog supply. Manitoba Pork, which sells more than 80 percent of hogs produced in Manitoba, scrapped its one-price-for-all formula Jan 31 when its contract with packers ended.
That resulted in layoffs at Manitoba's smallest packer earlier this month because a purchase price could not be agreed upon to maintain supply.
Manitoba Agriculture Minister Harry Enns brokered a deal Feb 6 that saw Manitoba Pork reinstitute the old formula until Friday to give it and packers time to agree to a new formula.
Negotiations on the new pricing plan continued on Tuesday, a government spokesman said.
"As far as we know, they're still talking," Manitoba government spokesman, Roger Matas said.
Officials at Maple Leaf and Manitoba Pork were not available for comment.
The next largest packer, Schneider Corp, had not issued layoff notices, the UFCW's Keith said.
